154: [edit] It is forbidden to anoint onself [with oil], even just part of the body and even if it is only to remove sweat. However, if one is sick, even if not in danger, or if one has scabs on their head, it is permitted.

[edit] It is prohibited to wear leather sandals or shoes. This even applies to the prosthetic of an amputee or the like. Even something that is made of wood but covered in leather is forbidden. If they are made of silk, straw, cloth, or other material, it is permitted even to go out in public wearing them. (And it is permitted to stand on leather pillows and sheets, though one who is stringent will receive blessings (Mordechai on Yoma and Trumat Hadeshen 149).)
[edit] A woman who has given birth is permitted to wear shoes for thirty days. A sick person is similar even if not in danger. The same applies to somebody who has an injured foot.

[edit] Anybody is permitted to wear shoes to avoid scorpions or the like to avoid getting bitten if there are scorpions or other biting things around. Rem"a: If rain fell and somebody gots to get from their home to synagogue or vice versa and they are delicate, they are permitted to wear shoes until they arrive (Mahari"l).
